title: Grade 2 Science — Thu, May 28
description: Animals Around Us — Day 4 of 5: Animal homes and body parts
subject: science

questions.question: Where does a bird live?
questions.explanation: Birds build nests — usually in trees or high places. They lay eggs and raise their babies there.

questions.question: Where do fish live?
questions.explanation: Fish live in water — rivers, ponds, lakes, or the ocean.

questions.question: Where does a lion live?
questions.explanation: Lions live in a den — a sheltered place like a cave or thick bushes.

questions.question: Where does a rabbit live?
questions.explanation: Rabbits live in burrows — tunnels they dig underground. This keeps them safe from predators.

questions.question: What does a spider build to catch food?
questions.explanation: Spiders spin webs from silk. Insects get stuck in the web and the spider eats them.

questions.question: What body part helps birds fly?
questions.explanation: Birds have wings covered in feathers that let them fly. Different birds have different-sized wings.

questions.question: What body part helps fish swim?
questions.explanation: Fish use their fins and tail to swim and steer through water. They also have gills to breathe.

questions.question: Which animal builds a dam across a river?
questions.explanation: Beavers build dams across rivers using sticks and mud. They live in a lodge (home) in the water.

questions.question: Which body part does a snake use to sense danger?
questions.explanation: Snakes flick their tongues to pick up chemical signals — it helps them smell and sense their surroundings.

questions.question: What covers a fish's body?
questions.explanation: Fish are covered in scales — small, overlapping plates that protect their body.

questions.question: What covers a bird's body?
questions.explanation: Birds are covered in feathers. Feathers keep them warm, help them fly, and can be very colorful.

questions.question: Where does a bee live?
questions.explanation: Bees live in a hive — a home made of hexagonal wax cells. They store honey there.

questions.question: What body part do elephants use to drink water and pick up food?
questions.explanation: An elephant's trunk is like a very long nose. It uses it to breathe, drink water, pick up food, and even communicate.

questions.question: What do we call the home of a dog?
questions.explanation: A dog's home is called a kennel. Trained dogs may have a kennel outside or sleep indoors.

questions.question: Which body covering is unique to mammals?
questions.explanation: Mammals have fur or hair. Cats, dogs, lions, elephants — all mammals have some hair on their bodies.
